description: Attention mechanism decomposed. Q, K, V projections. Scaled dot-product attention. Softmax normalization. Multi-head splitting + concatenation. Flash attention's tiled computation. Efficient variants: linear attention, sparse attention, ring attention.

sub_mechanisms.name: query_key_value_projection
sub_mechanisms.definition: Q = X @ W_q, K = X @ W_k, V = X @ W_v. Three learnable linear projections of input.
sub_mechanisms.why: Q: 'what am I looking for'. K: 'what do I have'. V: 'what do I contribute'. Separable roles per head. Foundational decomposition.

sub_mechanisms.name: scaled_dot_product
sub_mechanisms.definition: scores = Q @ K^T / √d_k. Each query's similarity to each key, scaled by √dim.
sub_mechanisms.why: Dot product = unscaled similarity. Without √d_k division, dot products grow with d_k → softmax saturates → vanishing gradient. The scaling is critical.

sub_mechanisms.name: attention_softmax
sub_mechanisms.definition: Apply softmax over keys: each row sums to 1. Soft selection mechanism.
sub_mechanisms.why: Convert scores to probabilities. Differentiable selection. Cost: softmax dominates attention numerics (exponentials, normalisation). Numerical care needed.

sub_mechanisms.name: attention_output
sub_mechanisms.definition: out = attention_weights @ V. Each query gets weighted sum of values.
sub_mechanisms.why: Weighted retrieval: attend to important keys, get their values. Per-query aggregation across context.

sub_mechanisms.name: multi_head_split
sub_mechanisms.definition: Split Q, K, V into H heads along feature dim. Compute attention per head. Concatenate.
sub_mechanisms.why: Different heads specialise (induction, copying, positional). Empirically gives more expressive attention than single head with same total dim.

sub_mechanisms.name: attention_quadratic_complexity
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compute QK^T over N tokens: N² × d operations. Memory: N² attention matrix.
sub_mechanisms.why: Fundamental cost. 100K context: 10^10 attention operations + 10^10 memory. The bottleneck for long context.

sub_mechanisms.name: flash_attention_tiling
sub_mechanisms.definition: Tile Q, K, V into blocks. Compute partial attention per tile; update online softmax.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard attention materialises N×N matrix (huge for large N). Flash never materialises it — computes attention output tile-by-tile. 2-3x faster + much less memory.

sub_mechanisms.name: online_softmax
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compute softmax over batches with running max + sum. Mathematically equivalent to global softmax.
sub_mechanisms.why: Key trick in Flash. Per-tile softmax + correction when seeing larger values. Without it, you'd need full attention matrix to normalise correctly.

sub_mechanisms.name: sparse_attention
sub_mechanisms.definition: Attend to only a subset of positions: sliding window, strided, local + global.
sub_mechanisms.why: Reduces N² to N×K for K-position sparsity pattern. Used in Longformer, BigBird, GPT-3 (some heads). Trade-off: information may not flow across sparse boundaries.

sub_mechanisms.name: linear_attention
sub_mechanisms.definition: Replace softmax with kernel feature map. Attention becomes φ(Q) @ (φ(K)^T @ V). O(N) per token.
sub_mechanisms.why: Linear in sequence length. Mamba, Linear Attention, Performer. Quality often below softmax attention but improving. Active research for long context.

sub_mechanisms.name: ring_attention
sub_mechanisms.definition: Distributed long-context attention: each device holds tile of K, V; rotates through ring; computes partial attention.
sub_mechanisms.why: Scale context beyond single-device memory. Used in Gemini, Claude long context. Each device sees all K, V over the ring rotation. Communication-bound.

sub_mechanisms.name: attention_score_interpretation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Visualise softmax weights: which tokens attend to which. Used for interpretability research.
sub_mechanisms.why: Hopeful but limited. Patterns emerge (induction heads, copying heads) but attention isn't directly = computation. The substrate's Tracr-authored networks have attention computing exact operations.

derivation_rules.name: scaled_attention_prevents_softmax_saturation
if: dot products are not scaled by √d_k
then: large d_k leads to softmax saturation and vanishing gradients
derivation_rules.why: Dot product of random vectors grows as √d. Unscaled scores get large → softmax peaks → gradient ~0. √d_k scaling keeps scores in manageable range. Mathematical necessity.

derivation_rules.name: flash_attention_avoids_materialising_N_squared_matrix
then: memory cost is O(N) instead of O(N²)
derivation_rules.why: Naive attention stores N×N attention scores. Flash never stores them — works tile-by-tile. For N=100K: 40 GB → 800 KB. Enables long-context that was impossible before.

derivation_rules.name: multi_head_more_expressive_than_single_head
if: attention is split into H heads with same total dim
then: expressivity is greater than single head
derivation_rules.why: Different heads can learn different relationships (syntactic, semantic, position). Empirically: better than single attention with same parameter count. Inductive bias toward decomposable attention.

derivation_rules.name: softmax_quadratic_is_long_context_bottleneck
then: compute + memory scale O(N²) with context
derivation_rules.why: Foundational. 100K context: 10 GFLOPs per token at typical d. Long context requires either Flash (constant factor wins) or efficient attention (asymptotic wins).

derivation_rules.name: linear_attention_recovers_O_N_at_quality_cost
if: softmax replaced by kernel feature map
then: attention is O(N) per token but quality typically drops
derivation_rules.why: Linear attention loses some softmax properties (sharpness, copy ability). Active research closing the gap. Mamba-style state-space models show promise as full softmax alternative.
